title: Deep Learning Examples
description: Small Deep Learning examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Start with a weighted input
examples.description: A weight controls how strongly an input affects a calculation. A bias is a number added afterward. A neural network combines many such calculations.
examples.code:
input_value = 3
weight = 2
bias = 1
print(input_value * weight + bias)

examples.title: Combine two features
examples.description: One unit can combine several inputs. Multiply each input by its own weight, add the products, then add the bias.
examples.code:
inputs = [2, 3]
weights = [4, 1]
bias = 1
value = sum(x * w for x, w in zip(inputs, weights)) + bias
print(value)

examples.title: An activation changes the shape
examples.description: An activation applies a chosen rule after a weighted sum. ReLU keeps positive numbers and changes negative numbers to zero.

examples.title: Make a small layer
examples.description: A layer is a group of units that work on the same incoming values. Two units can produce two outputs from one input.
examples.code:
x = 3
first = max(0, x * 2 + 1)
second = max(0, x * -1 + 1)
print([first, second])

examples.title: Connect layers in order
examples.description: A later layer uses the earlier layer outputs as its inputs. Deep networks have several layers that transform information step by step.

examples.title: Use shape to check connections
examples.description: Shape describes how values are arranged. For a batch, each row is one example. A layer must receive the number of features it expects.

examples.title: Loss measures a mistake
examples.description: A loss is a number that measures how wrong a prediction is. Squared error multiplies the difference by itself.

examples.title: A slope points toward a change
examples.description: A slope describes how quickly a value changes nearby. For the loss (weight - 3) squared, its slope is twice (weight - 3).

examples.title: Take one learning step
examples.description: The learning rate sets how big a weight update is. Subtracting a small amount in the slope direction can reduce the loss.
examples.code:
weight = 5.0
rate = 0.1
slope = 2 * (weight - 3)
weight = weight - rate * slope
print(round(weight, 2))

examples.title: Backpropagation follows the links
examples.description: Backpropagation finds how each weight affects the loss by following the calculation links backward. Libraries handle this bookkeeping for large networks.
examples.code:
Forward: input -> hidden layer -> output -> loss
Backward: loss -> output weights -> hidden weights
Update: use each weight slope to make a small change

examples.title: Batches and epochs
examples.description: A batch is a small group of examples processed together. An epoch is one pass through the training set. More passes do not guarantee a better test result.
examples.code:
Training set: 12 examples
Batch size: 4 examples
One epoch: 3 batches
Two epochs: 6 batches in total

examples.title: Check before trusting a network
examples.description: Training, validation and test sets have different jobs. Validation helps choose settings. The final test checks a choice that has already been made.
examples.code:
Training: adjust weights
Validation: choose settings and when to stop
Test: report the final check
Report: describe errors and data limits
